quotes.text: After you’ve enabled and integrated it, Stripe automatically displays Link to your customers for eligible transactions.
It doesn’t support advanced acquiring features
Passing `link` in the `allowed_payment_method_types` parameter always treats Link as a payment method, even if you also pass `card`.
Stripe recommends identifying non-card payments as Link payments instead of rendering the fixed values.

old_evidence.text: If the customer approves the backup, and the initial payment attempt fails, Link automatically retries the payment using the backup.
To include Link in a card integration, pass `card` in the `payment_method_types` parameter.

findings: The November capture is a complete two-route guide. Both captures require Wallets Dashboard enablement and appropriate integration before automatic display for eligible transactions. Both paths may represent card and eligible alternative funding including Instant Bank Payments and Klarna, subject to the specific method/surface. Standalone Link returns `PaymentMethod.type=link`; card-specific Link returns `type=card`, `card.wallet.type=link` (old raw lines 8-23,29-37, new raw lines 9-24,33-41).

Source lines 17–25 and Link concept lines 18–25 document the May `payment_method_types` request. Preserve it as dated and add the November `allowed_payment_method_types` route. Both versions say putting `link` in the respective parameter wins even alongside `card`; the card-specific route includes `card` while omitting `link` (old raw lines 19-37, new raw lines 20-41). Separately, the 2026-07-29.dahlia Intent changelog documents compatible-subset filtering and mutual exclusion with the old, excluded, automatic and configuration controls (`raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-07-29-allowed-payment-method-types-parameter-2026-11-07.md:7-21,25-29`). The named 2026-09-30.endive endpoints and REST table remove writes for PaymentIntent create/update/confirm and SetupIntent create/update, return 400 `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported` for those writes and retain the response property. That changelog's Impact section instead names `2026-08-26.preview`, so do not infer wider version behavior (`raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:7-36`). The separate Checkout Link guide still lists both card and link with the older field, including in November, while the Endive Checkout Session create changelog removes it as a request but retains it as response. Scope the hosted Checkout concept at lines 81–87 and route the reciprocal warning (`raw/stripe-payments-link-checkout-link-2026-11-07.md:26-57`, `raw/stripe-checkout-link-2025.md:25-38,62-78`, `raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:7-23`). No cross-environment parameter substitution: the separate Endive Stripe.js deferred Elements surface uses camel-case `allowedPaymentMethodTypes` for client configuration (`raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-elements-deferred-intent-payment-method-types-2026-11-07.md:7-17`).

The November guide adds an explicit exclusion of extended authorization, incremental authorization and overcapture for the standalone Link payment-method route, alongside the retained single blended-rate/no-IC+ description (old raw lines 23-27, new raw lines 24-31). The guide points affected readers to the card-specific route. This change documents the standalone restriction and does not establish newly revoked support, card-route feature availability for a particular payment, or pricing entitlement. The retained online feature guides scope availability by network, merchant, configuration and where applicable the Charge status (`raw/stripe-extended-authorization-2026.md:14-30`, `raw/stripe-incremental-authorization-2026.md:16-32`, `raw/stripe-overcapture-2026.md:16-28,149`). Add the explicit restrictions in the source and reciprocal Link concept.

Both integration captures describe PaymentMethod representation and say the standalone Link objects do not show how the customer paid. Separately, the November Link payment-methods guide says the Charge can expose a funding source group in `payment_method_details.link.funding_source_group` or `payment_method_details.card.wallet.link.funding_source_group`, respectively. The group can cover more than one instrument type, such as Pix and UPI, and is distinct from exact funding instrument or card metadata. It also describes group fees according to the Stripe Pricing Agreement, which should remain scoped alongside the main guide's single blended-rate wording (old raw lines 21-23,31-45 and new raw lines 22-24,35-49; `raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-methods-2026-11-07.md:11-54`). The related May guide uses the same dashboard label but its inspected eligibility section does not document group metadata (`raw/stripe-link-payment-methods-2025.md:12-30`). Avoid equating funding opacity on PaymentMethod with no group metadata on Charge.

Both integration captures say immediate confirmation and successful-payment settlement to the Stripe balance on the card timeline (old raw line 8, new raw line 9). Keep that documented general description separate from bank payout, underlying-method eligibility and outcome. The November Instant Bank Payments guide confirms authorized payments settle on that timeline, with the customer-bank dispute exception, and gives US account and integration boundaries (`raw/stripe-payments-link-instant-bank-payments-2026-11-07.md:8-13,105-137`). The separate Klarna-on-Link guide scopes supported US surfaces to Payment Links, hosted Checkout and Payment Element, and describes a full purchase-amount credit minus fees to the Stripe account immediately after issuer authorization. Preserve that timing as specific dated wording alongside the general card-timeline wording, without turning it or the Link concept's line 48 into a bank-payout promise (`raw/stripe-payments-link-klarna-2026-11-07.md:8-17,55-64`).

Baseline source line 26 and Link concept line 25 omit conditions. Link only suggests the backup for multiple eligible saved sources, and it automatically retries after customer approval and initial failure only in the standalone path. The card-specific route has no backup selection (old raw lines 23-27,83-87, new raw lines 24-26,89-93). An approved backup or retry does not establish successful payment.
substantive_changes: The manual request field changes from May `payment_method_types` to November `allowed_payment_method_types` for standalone and card-specific routing, with dynamic payment methods still supported and the same Link precedence (old raw lines 19-35, new raw lines 20-39).

November adds explicit standalone-Link exclusions for extended authorization, incremental authorization and overcapture. The IC+ blended-rate limitation persists (old raw lines 25-27, new raw lines 26-31).
Heading whitespace and JSON formatting are presentation-only, retaining the same sample values and topology (diff lines 7-8,37-56; old raw lines 37-83, new raw lines 41-89).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Date May 8 and November 7 guidance. Retain Dashboard/eligibility prerequisites, dynamic versus configured choices, PaymentMethod representation, both funding options and the suggest/approve/failure conditions on standby payment, plus successful-payment Stripe-balance timing (old raw lines 1-37,83-87 and new raw lines 1-41,89-93).

For card-specific Link, actual credit/debit funding retains card details. For non-card funding keep fixed `brand=link`, network `link`, `last4=0000`, `12/2040`, unknown funding, other display brand and null checks as documented placeholders. Show the Link label in customer-facing UI (old raw lines 31-85, new raw lines 35-91).

Add Wallets enablement/automatic eligible display, all supported funding with method/surface restrictions, conditional backup, group-discriminator versus exact source detail, and confirmation versus settlement boundary. The current summary omits these or is categorical at lines 17–26. The reciprocal Link route resolves at Stripe index lines 455 and 736 and concept lines 12–34,81–87,183.

source_assessments.reason: The new Link guide substantively changes documented manual API configuration and adds important route limitations. The existing summary has unqualified request and retry rules and should route readers to the related endpoint and eligibility distinctions.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/link-payment-integrations requires enabling Link under Wallets and integrating it for the use case. Stripe then shows it for eligible transactions (new raw lines 9-16). The recommended standalone route uses dynamic payment methods or includes `link` in `allowed_payment_method_types` and returns `PaymentMethod.type=link`. If eligible saved sources are multiple, Link can suggest a backup. After customer approval, it retries that backup if the first attempt fails. The route uses blended pricing and excludes IC+, extended authorization, incremental authorization and overcapture (new raw lines 20-31). The card integration includes `card` and omits `link` from the allow list, since `link` takes precedence even alongside `card`. It returns `type=card` and `card.wallet.type=link` and offers no checkout backup. Genuine credit or debit funding retains card details, while eligible non-card funding has values such as brand `link` and last four `0000`, which Stripe says to label Link in the UI (new raw lines 33-91). Both routes allow eligible Link funding including Instant Bank Payments and Klarna, with method and surface restrictions. The guide describes immediate confirmation and card-timeline settlement of successful payments to the Stripe balance (new raw lines 9-16). The May capture and source-stripe-link-payment-integrations.md used `payment_method_types`, preserved the PaymentMethod distinction, and did not give the newer acquiring exclusions. The current summary also omits the consent and failure conditions for a backup (old raw lines 8-37 and old raw lines 83-87).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/link-payment-integrations, the substantive November changes are the manual request field `allowed_payment_method_types` in both routes and the three acquiring exclusions for standalone Link, with IC+ still excluded (old raw lines 19-35 and new raw lines 20-39). Heading and JSON formatting changes retain the sample values (old raw lines 37-83 and new raw lines 41-89). source-stripe-link-payment-integrations.md and the Link concept should date May's `payment_method_types`, preserve Link precedence, and link the separate API boundaries. Dahlia's 2026-07-29 Intent reference filters to the compatible subset and makes the allowed list mutually exclusive with the old field, excluded list, automatic field, and payment-method configuration. The named 2026-09-30.endive Intent endpoints reject old writes with HTTP 400 `payment_method_types_no_longer_supported` and retain the response property. The separately retained November Checkout Link's old-field recipe conflicts for Endive Checkout Session creation, and deferred Elements uses client-side `allowedPaymentMethodTypes`, a separate surface (`raw/stripe-changelog-dahlia-2026-07-29-allowed-payment-method-types-parameter-2026-11-07.md:7-21`, `raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:7-36`, `raw/stripe-payments-link-checkout-link-2026-11-07.md:51-57`, `raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:7-23`, `raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-elements-deferred-intent-payment-method-types-2026-11-07.md:7-17`). Both captures preserve eligible display, conditional backup, and genuine versus placeholder card data. The separate guide documents coarse Charge metadata under `payment_method_details.link.funding_source_group` for the standalone route and `payment_method_details.card.wallet.link.funding_source_group` for the card route. This is distinct from exact funding and card details on the PaymentMethod. Keep the specific US-only Klarna surface and credit-after-authorization wording and Instant Bank Payments dispute exception alongside the general balance-settlement statement (`raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-methods-2026-11-07.md:29-54`, `raw/stripe-payments-link-klarna-2026-11-07.md:8-17,57-64`, `raw/stripe-payments-link-instant-bank-payments-2026-11-07.md:105-137`). The card integration route does not establish acquiring eligibility or an actual payment or bank payout.
